answer: Divergent-Answer Gate. Each agent must answer a random challenge whose correct response depends on its private, evolving local history. Honest agents diverge naturally; clones share one history and return identical replies. The gate compares replies through a prism that splits each answer into independent features, and any matching pair is denied a wharf slot for the next task round. A rotating beacon picks the challenge, so attackers cannot precompute. Cost: every clone must maintain and pay for its own distinct history, turning one identity into N full identities.
